Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "161 :     public void flush() throws IOException {\n162 :         flush(true); \n163 :     }"

Diagnosis:
The failing test `testBase64EmptyOutputStream` expects that encoding an empty input (new byte[0]) produces an empty encoded output. However, the bug report notes that encoding an empty byte array actually produces a CRLF (carriage return + line feed) sequence instead of an empty output.

Looking into the Base64OutputStream class, the write method delegates to the internal Base64 codec to encode or decode the given bytes. The key behavior occurs in Base64OutputStream.close(), which notifies the encoder of EOF by calling base64.encode(singleByte, 0, -1). This signals the Base64 instance that no more input remains and to finalize the encoding.

Within Base64.encode(byte[], int, int), when inAvail < 0 (EOF) and there is no input (modulus 0), the encoder appends padding characters (=) and then appends the line separator (e.g., CRLF) if lineLength > 0. This means even when input is empty, it adds a lineSeparator at EOF during the flush triggered by close().

Therefore, when encoding an empty input, the final output is not empty but contains the line separator bytes (CRLF). This is because the current implementation always writes the lineSeparator in the EOF case if lineLength > 0, regardless of input length.

This behavior explains the test failure: the test expects an empty array from Base64 encoding of empty input, but it actually gets a CRLF sequence appended by the Base64 encoder upon EOF handling.

The relevant bug stems from the EOF handling in Base64.encode: improperly appending a line separator (CRLF) when no actual encoded bytes exist (empty input). The fix would be to avoid appending lineSeparator during EOF if no data was encoded before.

Recent bug reports do not pertain to this issue, so they can be ignored for this diagnosis.

In summary:
- The test checks encoding empty input produces empty output.
- Base64.encode on empty input appends CRLF due to EOF lineSeparator appending.
- This causes test failure and the bug report symptom.
- Modifying EOF handling in Base64.encode to avoid lineSeparator if no data encoded will fix it.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
